findings.title: Re-run test expects an unchanged target, but the retention window moves with session age
findings.recommendation: Task 5.6 says a re-run leaves the 'target unchanged'. Under the new retention rule (cleanupPeriodDays = max(existing, oldest age + 365)), a re-run on a later day computes a larger needed value and rewrites settings.json, which the No-overwrite requirement permits. Reword 5.6 to 'no chat data, file history or code copied, and those unchanged on the target' so it matches the spec's Re-run scenario.

walk_entry.title: A fixed 365-day retention window does not protect every moved session

findings.title: 'Directories shown' scenario assumes the target home without stating it
findings.recommendation: The scenario expects the target slug -home-sal-code-home-env, which holds only if the target's home is /home/sal; the WHEN clause names only `--remote fedora`. Add 'and the target home is /home/sal' to the WHEN so a test author need not infer it, as the Linux target scenario already does.

walk_entry.title: A counts-only plan cannot meet the stage's 'exact file set' exit criterion

commentary: Verified the two walks against the live artifacts and the architecture doc. Every edited file is in some entry's edit record, strict validation passes, and no markers remain. The resolutions are present at every site they claim; the retired wording (dry-run flag, fixed 365, outside-home --skip-code exception, counts-only plan) is gone from the change and the doc. The two residual nits are both second-order effects of this walk's own decisions: the computed retention window makes a re-run's settings write legitimate, which one test line still forbids, and the new confirmation scenario borrows an unstated target home. Neither changes the design.
